review_text: TL;DR: Great game, worse Hollow Knight. 8/10 For context: the original Hollow Knight is my favorite game of all time. I've beaten it deathless and without upgrading my character. So when I say Silksong frustrated me, it's not a skill issue rant. If Hollow Knight gives you a wall and tells you to go find a pickaxe, Silksong expects you to break through it with your head. The good Movement is god-tier. Hornet glides through levels like a ballerina. Traversal is so fluid it's basically its own form of fun, so the huge map never feels like a chore to cross. Combat has depth. Pogo, parries, deflecting projectiles, tools (spears, knives, potions, grenades), and Crests that completely change your moveset or healing. You can build a mage, a tool spammer, whatever you want. Exploring new areas is the best part. Almost every biome brings new enemies, mechanics and upgrades. Greymoor, Shellwood, Deep Docks and the Citadel are phenomenal, classic Metroidvania design. Art and music are stunning. Tons of tiny details, multilayered backgrounds, and another incredible Christopher Larkin soundtrack. Story and lore are coherent and well thought out, and Hornet actually talking makes the narrative much easier to follow. The bad Less Metroidvania, more Souls. Many areas are fairly linear with shortcuts. You clear them on the first pass and never come back. Backtracking often leads to a room with a handful of rosaries. Some secrets are absurdly hidden , Dark Souls illusory wall style. Good luck getting 100% without a guide. The balance feels like a stream challenge run. HK's endgame damage (2 masks per hit) becomes the default a few hours in, while your HP stays at base level. Getting knocked into spikes by a boss can take 4 masks in a second. The new healing (3 masks at once, but only with full silk) is the only thing that makes this work. If you get chunked with no silk, you need 9 hits on 1 HP to heal. Stingy direct progression. Twice as many silk upgrades as HK for the same endpoint. Your first needle upgrade is basically it until Act 2. One extra mask barely matters when you die in 3 hits anyway. "Rage-game" design. A bench that's a trap (the only one in the whole game, using the same assets), a boss that explodes on death and nearly one-shots you, flying enemies that fall on you for double damage. Consequences way out of proportion to the mistake. Gauntlets everywhere. Locked-arena wave fights every 15 minutes against enemies you've already beaten, often copy-pasted arenas, often with no reward at all (drops disabled). One mandatory 10-wave gauntlet ends in a boss, so every death means 10 more minutes to try again. Lazy bosses. Few of them, many with 2 to 4 attacks spammed at high speed and high damage. Lots of them spawn random adds, so RNG decides how hard the fight is. Some are recycled up to three times as mandatory fights. Broken economy. Paid benches are fine (rosary strings exist for that), but shop prices are huge and about half the enemies drop nothing. You WILL farm rosaries, and shell shards too if you rely on tools. Little to no rewards. Many bosses give nothing, one 30-minute area gives you... a Steam achievement. Clearing a zone for an hour gets you 30 rosaries. For a game with speedrun and deathless achievements, this kills replay value. Quests are MMO-style fetch/kill tasks, a leftover from when Silksong was a DLC, and they're mandatory to reach the endgame. Courier quests are basically mini platforming Death Stranding: you'll either love them or hate them. Minor bugs : bosses vanishing between phases and just dying, broken scripts, inconsistent hitboxes. Rare, and the devs are patching quickly. Act 3 (spoilers) Story-wise it's great fanservice that ties up most threads from HK. Lace's arc feels chaotic and underexplained, and Grandmother Silk appears in like two scenes, so the antagonist never really lands. Gameplay-wise, the jump to the endgame is barely noticeable because the whole game already had endgame balance. Most side bosses give nothing or near-useless items. And the final boss of a multi-dozen-hour game is... a third Lace fight with extra AoE attacks, partly recycled from other enemies. Seriously? The whole act feels rushed and done on the cheap: barely any new areas, recycled enemies, and the difficulty bump is just the same modifiers slapped on everything. Verdict The core gameplay is impeccable, and most of the problems show up only when you dig into the details, so you might not even notice them. This is for HK veterans who want a bigger challenge and Souls fans who like platformers. If you're new to hard games, it might break you. Hollow Knight is a 9/10 for me. Silksong is an 8/10 , and at its price it's still one of the biggest, highest-quality games you can buy.

I beat the first main boss 3 times now and whenever I go to call it a night, the game will go to a black screen and bam, hours of progress is gone. I even managed to unlock the Crusader but now he's gone too. Words cannot describe how disappointing and heartbreaking this is. I believe the devs will be pretty on top of this issue (hopefully) but as of right now, I would wait to pick this up until this issue is fixed.
